hypotheses.reasoning: Trigger: template-svc-1 was restarted by a failed liveness probe at 16:10:28 (#1092), dropping capacity to 3/4. Before that, template-svc was healthy (GC normal, renders ~20-90ms, #1087). Amplification: notification-svc's TemplateClient retries 503s immediately with backoff disabled (#1137 attempt 2/4, #1164 retry 3/4 with 0ms delay, #1205 attempt 4/4). Those retries pile onto the remaining template-svc instances, which hit 590 in-flight (3.2x normal) and began load-shedding (#1187, #1212, #1234, inflight 827). Gateway 503s follow (#1186, #1300, #1356, #1474) as retries are exhausted. The stall persists because the immediate retries keep the load above capacity. The loss of one instance was survivable alone; the zero-backoff retries turned it into a sustained outage. The liveness-probe cause itself is not visible in these logs (heap and GC look normal).

Alternative reading: template-svc-1 may have hung before the liveness failure, making template-svc a slow dependency for notification-svc. The logs show no hang or timeout from template-svc before #1092, so this is weakly supported. The status-poller timeouts against legacy-inventory (#299, #593, #1513) are a separate deprecated endpoint and do not affect the notify path.

verdict.recommendedAction: Enable exponential backoff with jitter and a retry cap on notification-svc's TemplateClient, and check its circuit breaker. Scale template-svc back to 4+ instances and confirm the restarted pod is healthy. Investigate why the template-svc liveness probe failed at 16:10:28 (probe timeout vs. real hang). Ignore the status-poller legacy-inventory timeouts for this incident: they are a separate deprecated-endpoint health check that is not on the /v1/notify path.

hypotheses.reasoning: Trigger: template-svc-1 was restarted by a failed liveness probe at 16:10:28 (#1092), dropping capacity to 3/4. Before that, template-svc was healthy (GC normal, renders ~20-90ms, #1087). Amplification: notification-svc's TemplateClient retries 503s immediately with backoff disabled (#1137 attempt 2/4, #1164 retry 3/4 with 0ms delay, #1205 attempt 4/4). Those retries pile onto the remaining template-svc instances, which hit 590 in-flight (3.2x normal) and began load-shedding (#1187, #1212, #1234, inflight 827). Gateway 503s follow (#1186, #1300, #1356, #1474) as retries are exhausted. The stall persists because the immediate retries keep the load above capacity. The loss of one instance was survivable alone; the zero-backoff retries turned it into a sustained outage. The liveness-probe cause itself is not visible in these logs (heap and GC look normal).
hypotheses.recommendedAction: Enable exponential backoff with jitter and a retry cap on notification-svc's TemplateClient, and check its circuit breaker. Scale template-svc back to 4+ instances and confirm the restarted pod is healthy. Investigate why the template-svc liveness probe failed at 16:10:28 (probe timeout vs. real hang). Ignore the status-poller legacy-inventory timeouts for this incident: they are a separate deprecated-endpoint health check that is not on the /v1/notify path.

The status-poller timeouts against legacy-inventory (#299, #593, #1513) are a separate deprecated endpoint and do not affect the notify path.
